body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].16) Having attached a mark to the left leg of a black bird, [placing] a sacrificial cake on the mark, with '<s>pra patetaḥ</s>' [AV 7.115], he sends it forth uncovered.

body.text: (KauśS_3,1[18].17) nīlaṃ saṃdhāya lohitam āchādya śuklaṃ pariṇahya dvitīyayā_uṣṇīṣam aṅkena_upasādya savyena sahāṅkenāvāṅ apsu_apavidhyati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].17) Having joined a blue [cloth], covered with a red one, bound around with a white one, with a second [cloth] having placed a turban with a mark, with the left [hand] together with the mark he casts [it] downward into the waters.
(KauśS_3,1[18].18) With the third [cloth it is] concealed, with the fourth enveloped.
(KauśS_3,1[18].19) Of the first, the variegated rite.

body.text: (KauśS_3,1[18].20) kulāyaśṛtaṃ [ed. kulāya ś-, but cf. Caland Kl. Schr. 58] haritabarhiṣam aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].20) He eats [food] cooked in a nest-[shaped vessel] on green <s>barhis</s> grass.
(KauśS_3,1[18].21) He places anointed [sticks] measuring a span.

body.text: (KauśS_3,1[18].22) nāvyayoḥ sāṃvaidye paścād agner bhūmiparilekhe kīlālaṃ mukhenāśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].22) At the two new-moon [rites], in the <s>sāṃvaidya</s> (communal offering), behind the fire, in an incision in the ground, he eats <s>kīlāla</s> (a sweet drink) with his mouth.
(KauśS_3,1[18].23) He eats the <s>tejovrata</s> (radiance-vow food) for three nights.
(KauśS_3,1[18].24) That is his food.

body.text: (KauśS_3,1[18].25) śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ [1.5 + 1.6]> <brahma jajñānam [4.1.1]> <asya vāmasya [9.9]> <yo rohito [13.1.25]> <ud asya ketavo [13.2.1]> <mūrdhāhaṃ [16.3.1]> <viṣāsahim [17.1.1-5]> iti salilaiḥ kṣīraudanam aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].25) With [the hymns] '<s>śaṃbhu-mayobhu</s>' [AV 1.5 + 1.6], '<s>brahma jajñānam</s>' [AV 4.1.1], '<s>asya vāmasya</s>' [AV 9.9], '<s>yo rohito</s>' [AV 13.1.25], '<s>ud asya ketavo</s>' [AV 13.2.1], '<s>mūrdhāham</s>' [AV 16.3.1], '<s>viṣāsahim</s>' [AV 17.1.1-5], he eats rice-milk [prepared] with the waters.
(KauśS_3,1[18].26) [The rites] ending with the <s>mantha</s> (stirred drink).
(KauśS_3,1[18].27) With the second [hymn], when about to travel, he should offer the <s>havis</s> (oblation).
(KauśS_3,1[18].28) Then, upon returning,
(KauśS_3,1[18].29) then, upon returning,
(KauśS_3,1[18].30) then, when seeking,
(KauśS_3,1[18].31) then, when seeking,
(KauśS_3,1[18].32) There are four holders of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) sticks.
(KauśS_3,1[18].33) Four of <s>darbha</s> grasses with winnowing baskets.
(KauśS_3,1[18].34) Having placed the interlocked eight-layered fuel-wood upon the <s>sāttrika</s> fire, he should offer with ghee.
(KauśS_3,1[18].35) He should restrain the smoke.
(KauśS_3,1[18].36) He should eat the residue.

body.text: (KauśS_3,1[18].37) tam u cen na vinded atha sattrasyāyatane yajñāyatanam iva kṛtvā
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,1[18].37) If he should not find that, then having made a sacrificial ground like a <s>sattra</s> session ground,
(KauśS_3,1[18].38) they call the rite '<s>samudra</s>' (ocean).

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].1) <ambayo yanty [1.4.1]> śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ [1.5 + 1.6] <brahma jajñānam [4.1]> <ā gāvo [4.21.1]> <ekā ca me [5.15.1]> iti gā lavaṇaṃ pāyayaty upatāpinīḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].1) With '<s>ambayo yanty</s>' [AV 1.4.1], '<s>śaṃbhu-mayobhu</s>' [AV 1.5 + 1.6], '<s>brahma jajñānam</s>' [AV 4.1], '<s>ā gāvo</s>' [AV 4.21.1], '<s>ekā ca me</s>' [AV 5.15.1], he gives salt-water to drink to the ailing cows.
(KauśS_3,2[19].2) [For those] desiring offspring.
(KauśS_3,2[19].3) He blocks the drinking trough.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].4) <saṃ saṃ sravantu [1.15.1]> iti nāvyābhyām udakam āharataḥ sarvata upāsecam
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].4) With '<s>saṃ saṃ sravantu</s>' [AV 1.15.1], with two new-moon [vessels] they bring water, sprinkling from all sides.
(KauśS_3,2[19].5) In that, he eats mixed grain cooked [in it].
(KauśS_3,2[19].6) Or <s>mantha</s> (stirred drink) mixed with curds and honey.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].7) yasya śriyaṃ kāmayate tato vrīhi_ājyapaya āhārya kṣīraudanam aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].7) From the person whose prosperity he desires, having brought rice, ghee, and milk, he eats rice-milk.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].8) tadalābhe haritagomayam āhārya śoṣayitvā trivṛti gomayaparicaye śṛtam aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].8) In the absence of that, having brought green cow-dung, having dried it, he eats [food] cooked in a triple cow-dung enclosure.
(KauśS_3,2[19].9) With '<s>śerabhaka</s>' [AV 2.24.1], the oceanic water rite has been explained.
(KauśS_3,2[19].10) Having gathered unhusked grain with a drop from a red she-goat, he eats.
(KauśS_3,2[19].11) This much he approaches.
(KauśS_3,2[19].12) Untying knots of grasses, he departs.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].13) tān udāvrajann udapātrasya_udapātreṇābhiplāvayati mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi [note conj. Speijer Museum 9 250]
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].13) Going up, he floods [the knots] from a water vessel with [another] water vessel, and wipes his face.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].14) <eha yantu paśavo [2.26.1]> <saṃ vo goṣṭhena [3.24.1]> <prajāvatīḥ [4.21.7 / 7.75]> <prajāpatir [6.11.3]> iti goṣṭhakarmāṇi
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].14) With '<s>eha yantu paśavo</s>' [AV 2.26.1], '<s>saṃ vo goṣṭhena</s>' [AV 3.24.1], '<s>prajāvatīḥ</s>' [AV 4.21.7 / 7.75], '<s>prajāpatir</s>' [AV 6.11.3], the cattle-pen rites.
(KauśS_3,2[19].15) He eats the first milk (<s>pīyūṣa</s>) of a cow that has calved, mixed with mucus.
(KauśS_3,2[19].16) He gives a cow.
(KauśS_3,2[19].17) He carries down the water vessel.
(KauśS_3,2[19].18) Having swept up, standing with the left [foot], he scatters half with the right [hand].

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].19) sārūpavatse śakṛtpiṇḍān guggululavaṇe pratinīya paścād agner nikhanati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].19) Having mixed dung-balls with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin) and salt for [a cow] with a same-colored calf, he buries [them] behind the fire.
(KauśS_3,2[19].20) Of the three [days], he eats in the morning.
(KauśS_3,2[19].21) When [something] has gone wrong, [it is considered] accomplished.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].22) <āyam agan [3.5.1]> <ayaṃ pratisaro [8.5.1]> <ayaṃ me varaṇo [10.3.1]> <arātīyor [10.6.1]> iti mantroktān vāsitān badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].22) With '<s>āyam agan</s>' [AV 3.5.1], '<s>ayaṃ pratisaro</s>' [AV 8.5.1], '<s>ayaṃ me varaṇo</s>' [AV 10.3.1], '<s>arātīyor</s>' [AV 10.6.1], he ties on the amulets mentioned in the <s>mantras</s>, having fumigated them.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].23) uttamasya caturo jātarūpaśakalenānusūtraṃ gamayitvāvabhujya traidhaṃ paryasyati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].23) Of the last, having threaded four [beads] with a piece of gold along the string, having bent [it], he wraps it around three times.
(KauśS_3,2[19].24) With '<s>etam idhmam</s>' [AV 10.6.35], having placed [fuel],

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].25) <tam imaṃ devatā [10.6.29]> iti vāsitam ullupya <brahmaṇā tejasā [10.6.30]> iti badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].25) with '<s>tam imaṃ devatā</s>' [AV 10.6.29], having fumigated the amulet, with '<s>brahmaṇā tejasā</s>' [AV 10.6.30], he ties it on.
(KauśS_3,2[19].26) With '<s>uttamo asi</s>' [AV 6.15.1], as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS_3,2[19].27) With '<s>akṣitās ta</s>' [AV 6.142.3], a barley-gem [amulet].

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].28) <prathamā ha vyuvāsa sā [3.10]> ity aṣṭakyāyā vapāṃ sarveṇa sūktena trir juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].28) With '<s>prathamā ha vyuvāsa sā</s>' [AV 3.10], he offers the omentum of a she-goat three times with the entire hymn of eight verses.
(KauśS_3,2[19].29) Of the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering) for those who are gathered together.

body.text: (KauśS_3,2[19].30) sahahutān ājyamiśrān hutvā paścād agner vāgyataḥ saṃviśati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,2[19].30) Having offered together with ghee the jointly-offered [portions], behind the fire, observing silence, he lies down.
(KauśS_3,2[19].31) Reciting the names of the great beings, he rises.
(KauśS_3,3[20].1) With '<s>sīrā yuñjanti</s>' [AV 3.17.1], he extends the yoke and plough.
(KauśS_3,3[20].2) He yokes the right draft-ox first.
(KauśS_3,3[20].3) With '<s>ehi pūrṇaka</s>' (Come, O Full One), the left one.
(KauśS_3,3[20].4) The ploughmen [yoke] the others.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].5) <aśvinā phālaṃ kalpayatām upāvatu bṛhaspatiḥ | yathāsad bahudhānyam ayakṣmaṃ bahupūruṣam [PS 8.18.6]> iti phālam atikarṣati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].5) With 'May the <s>Aśvins</s> prepare the ploughshare, may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> assist, so that there be abundant grain, freedom from disease, and many people' [PS 8.18.6], he ploughs with the ploughshare.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].6) <irāvān asi dhārtarāṣṭre tava me sattre rādhyatām [-]> iti pratimimīte
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].6) With 'You are <s>Irāvān</s> (the nourishing one), O son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, in your <s>sattra</s> (session) may [my goal] be accomplished,' he measures out [the field].
(KauśS_3,3[20].7) With '<s>apahatāḥ pratiṣṭhāḥ</s>' (Obstacles are struck away), having struck with cakes, he ploughs.
(KauśS_3,3[20].8) Having gone to the end of the hymn, he distributes.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].9) tisraḥ sītāḥ prācīr gamayanti kalyāṇīr vāco vadantaḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].9) They drive three furrows eastward, speaking auspicious words.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].10) <sīte vandāmahe tvā [3.17.8]> ity āvartayitvā_uttarasmin sītānte puroḍāśena_indraṃ yajate
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].10) With '<s>sīte vandāmahe tvā</s>' [AV 3.17.8], having turned around, at the end of the northern furrow, he worships <s>Indra</s> with a sacrificial cake.
(KauśS_3,3[20].11) The <s>Aśvins</s> with a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering).
(KauśS_3,3[20].12) They bring the remainders into the furrow.
(KauśS_3,3[20].13) The northern [remainders] into a water vessel.
(KauśS_3,3[20].14) Having placed the young-grass oblations,
(KauśS_3,3[20].15) he anoints everything.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].16) yatra saṃpātān ānayati tato loṣṭaṃ dhārayantaṃ patnī pṛchaty akṛkṣata_iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].16) Where they bring the remainders, from there the wife asks the one holding a clod of earth, 'Have you ploughed?'
(KauśS_3,3[20].17) 'We have ploughed.'
(KauśS_3,3[20].18) 'What did you bring?'

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].19) <vittiṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyam [cf. i.a. PS 5.35.1, PS 19.53.19? (= PSK 19.53.10)]> iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].19) 'Wealth, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, cattle, food, and sustenance' [cf. PS 5.35.1, PS 19.53.19].
(KauśS_3,3[20].20) He sows in the middle [furrow] from the north.
(KauśS_3,3[20].21) Having anointed, he stores the northern ploughshare for the morning yoking.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].22) sītāśiraḥsu darbhān āstīrya plakṣa_udumbarasya trīṃs_trīṃś camasān nidadhāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].22) Having spread <s>darbha</s> grass at the heads of the furrows, he places three cups each of <s>plakṣa</s> and <s>udumbara</s> wood.

body.text: (KauśS_3,3[20].23) rasavato dakṣiṇe śaṣpavato madhyame puroḍāśavata uttare
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,3[20].23) Those with juice in the southern [cup], those with young grass in the middle, those with sacrificial cake in the northern.
(KauśS_3,3[20].24) Having bent back the <s>darbha</s> grasses, he sows.
(KauśS_3,3[20].25) Having mixed dung-balls with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin) and salt for [a cow] with a same-colored calf, he eats.
(KauśS_3,3[20].26) The bull-prosperity [rite].
(KauśS_3,4[21].1) With '<s>payasvatīr</s>' [AV 3.24], the rite for prosperity.

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].2) śāntaphalaśilākṛtiloṣṭavalmīkarāśivāpaṃ trīṇi kūdīprāntāni madhyamapalāśe darbheṇa pariveṣṭya rāśipalyeṣu karoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].2) [Taking] a fruit, a stone, an earthen clod, [material from] an anthill, and a heap from the peaceful [ground], three ends of grain-heaps, having wrapped [them] with <s>darbha</s> grass on the middle <s>palāśa</s> leaf, he places [them] on the heap-covers.
(KauśS_3,4[21].3) They eat in the evening.
(KauśS_3,4[21].4) They sow back the remainder.
(KauśS_3,4[21].5) Until the food-distribution.
(KauśS_3,4[21].6) He consecrates with <s>mantras</s>.

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].7) <ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ [6.79]> iti palye_aśmānaṃ saṃprokṣyānvṛcaṃ kāśī opyāvāpayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].7) With '<s>ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ</s>' [AV 6.79], having sprinkled a stone on the heap-cover, verse by verse, he has the <s>Kāśī</s> [priest] sow.
(KauśS_3,4[21].8) With '<s>ā gāvo</s>' [AV 4.21], he stands up to greet the cows as they come.
(KauśS_3,4[21].9) In the rainy season, he offers three times to <s>Indra</s> from the first shower.
(KauśS_3,4[21].10) With <prajāvatīḥ []> he blesses (the cows) as they settle down

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].11) karkīpravādānāṃ dvādaśadāmnyāṃ saṃpātavatyām <ayaṃ ghāso ... iha vatsām [4.38.7cd]> iti mantroktam
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].11) In the <s>karkī</s>-proclamations, on the twelfth strand, with remainders, <ayaṃ ghāso ... iha vatsām [4.38.7cd]> — as stated in the mantra
(KauśS_3,4[21].12) With <yas te śokāya [5.1.3]> — for the attainment of garments

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].13) tisraḥ kūdīmayīr ūrṇanābhikulāya parihitā anvaktā ādadhāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].13) He places three (amulets) made of <s>kūdī</s> (plant), wound around and anointed, upon a spider's nest

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].14) atyanteṣīkāmauñjaparihitā [thus with Caland, AZ p. 55, n. 5] madhunā pralipya cikkaśeṣu paryasya
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].14) Wrapped with an <s>iṣīkā</s> (reed) and <s>muñja</s> (grass) band [thus with Caland, AZ p. 55, n. 5], having smeared with honey, he throws (them) among the <s>cikkaśa</s> (trees/thickets)
(KauśS_3,4[21].15) With <uta putraḥ [5.1.8]> he makes the eldest son sit down
(KauśS_3,4[21].16) One with measured shelter performs the rite of prosperity

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].17) <ardham ardhena [5.1.9]> ity ārdrapāṇir asaṃjñātvā [so Caland; ed. ārdrapāṇī rasaṃ jñātvā] prayachati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].17) With <ardham ardhena [5.1.9]>, with wet hands, without giving a signal [so Caland; ed. ārdrapāṇī rasaṃ jñātvā], he gives (the offering)
(KauśS_3,4[21].18) Having removed the forward part with a calmed branch
(KauśS_3,4[21].19) He sprinkles (water) around toward the fire
(KauśS_3,4[21].20) On the <s>amāvāsyā</s> (new moon) of that (month), he places three (pieces) of a span's measure
(KauśS_3,4[21].22) He performs the <s>rasakarman</s> (juice/essence rites)
(KauśS_3,4[21].22) He performs the <s>rasakarman</s> (juice/essence rites)

body.text: (KauśS_3,4[21].23) <stuṣva varṣman [5.2.7]> iti prājāpatyāmāvāsyāyām astamite valmīkaśirasi darbhāvastīrṇe_adhyadhi dīpaṃ dhārayaṃs trir juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,4[21].23) With <stuṣva varṣman [5.2.7]>, on the <s>Prājāpatya</s> <s>amāvāsyā</s> (new moon sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>), after sunset, on the head of an anthill spread with <s>darbha</s> (grass), holding a lamp on top, he offers oblations three times
(KauśS_3,4[21].24) Having brought rice-grain remainders, he pours juices over them and eats
(KauśS_3,4[21].25) Similarly on the full moon day, (he eats the remainders) mixed with ghee

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].1) <ṛdhaṅmantro [5.1]> <tad id āsa [5.2]> iti maiśradhānyaṃ bhṛṣṭapiṣṭaṃ lohitālaṃkṛtaṃ rasamiśram aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].1) With <ṛdhaṅmantro [5.1]> <tad id āsa [5.2]>, he eats mixed grains — roasted, ground, adorned with red (dye), mixed with <s>rasa</s> (juice/essence)

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].2) abhṛṣṭaṃ plakṣa_udumbarasya_uttarato_agnes triṣu camaseṣu pūrvāhṇasya tejasāgram annasya prāśiṣam iti pūrvāhṇe
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].2) Unroasted, to the north of the <s>Plakṣa</s> and <s>Udumbara</s> (trees), north of the fire, in three cups — 'With the splendor of the forenoon, the first portion of food for eating' — thus in the forenoon

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].3) madhyandinasya tejasā madhyam annasya prāśi.am iti madhyandine
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].3) 'With the splendor of midday, the middle portion of food for eating' — thus at midday

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].4) aparāhṇasya tejasā sarvam annasya prāśiṣam ity aparāhṇe
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].4) 'With the splendor of the afternoon, the entire portion of food for eating' — thus in the afternoon
(KauśS_3,5[22].5) With the fingers, the blood of a woman in her season

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].6) yat kṣetraṃ kāmayate tasmin kīlālaṃ dadhimadhumiśram
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].6) In whichever field he desires, (he pours) <s>kīlāla</s> (a sweet drink) mixed with curds and honey

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].7) saṃvatsaraṃ striyam anupetya śuktyāṃ reta ānīya taṇḍulamiśraṃ saptagrāmam
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].7) Having not approached a woman for a year, having brought semen in a shell, mixed with rice grains, (he distributes it) to seven villages

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].8) dvādaśīm amāvāsyā_iti kṣīrabhakṣo bhavaty amāvāsyāyāṃ dadhimadhubhakṣas tasya mūtre_udakadadhimadhupalpūlanāni_āsicya
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].8) The twelfth day and the <s>amāvāsyā</s> (new moon) — he subsists on milk; on the <s>amāvāsyā</s>, he subsists on curds and honey; he pours upon its urine water, curds, honey, and flour-cakes

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].9) <kravyādaṃ nāḍī pra viveśāgniṃ prajābhāṅgirato māyayaitau | āvāṃ devī juṣāṇe ghṛtācī imam annādyāya pra viśataṃ svāhā [-]> iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].9) <kravyādaṃ nāḍī pra viveśāgniṃ prajābhāṅgirato māyayaitau | āvāṃ devī juṣāṇe ghṛtācī imam annādyāya pra viśataṃ svāhā [-]>

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].10) niśāyām āgrayaṇataṇḍulān udakyān madhumiśrān nidadhāty ā yavānāṃ paṅkteḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].10) At night, he places <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits) rice grains, (gathered from a woman who is) impure, mixed with honey, up to the row of barley
(KauśS_3,5[22].11) Likewise with barley; having combined both
(KauśS_3,5[22].12) He eats (the preparation) cooked in a threefold cow-dung enclosure
(KauśS_3,5[22].13) 'It is complete/enriched' — thus says <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>

body.text: (KauśS_3,5[22].14) <mamāgne varco [5.3]> iti sāttrikān agnīn darbhapūtīkabhāṅgābhiḥ paristīrya gārhapatyaśṛtaṃ sarveṣu saṃpātavantaṃ gārhapatyadeśe_aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,5[22].14) With <mamāgne varco [5.3]>, having strewn around the <s>Sāttrika</s> fires with <s>darbha</s> (grass), <s>pūtīka</s> (plant), and <s>bhāṅgā</s> (hemp), he eats (the offering) cooked on the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (fire), with remainders (distributed) to all (fires), at the place of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>
(KauśS_3,5[22].15) Likewise, having gathered from the first (fire) to the other two
(KauśS_3,5[22].16) Likewise, the juices in a <s>droṇakalaśa</s> (trough-vessel) — as stated

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].1) <yajūṃṣi yajñe [5.26]> iti navaśālāyāṃ sarpir madhumiśram aśnāti [but Caland: juhoti]
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].1) With <yajūṃṣi yajñe [5.26]>, in a new hall, he eats (or offers [but Caland: juhoti]) clarified butter mixed with honey
(KauśS_3,6[23].2) With <doṣo gāya [6.1]>, the second (offering)
(KauśS_3,6[23].3) With the two 'yoked' (verses), the third
(KauśS_3,6[23].4) With the <s>Ānumatī</s> (verse), the fourth

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].5) śālām aṅgulibhyāṃ saṃprokṣya gṛhapatnyāsāda upaviśya_udapātraṃ ninayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].5) Having sprinkled the hall with the fingers, having sat down near the wife of the householder, he brings down a water vessel
(KauśS_3,6[23].6) With <ihaiva sta [7.60.7]> he releases speech

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].7) <ūrdhvā asya [5.27]> iti vārṣmaṇam audumbaraṃ manthapratirūpam abhijuhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].7) With <ūrdhvā asya [5.27]>, he offers an oblation of a <s>mantha</s> (stirred drink) likeness made of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree wood), of the height (of the person)
(KauśS_3,6[23].8) Having cooked innumerable (items), seven <s>śaṣkulī</s> (cakes) that have come together

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].9) <tvaṣṭā me []> iti prātar +vibhakṣyamāṇo [so Caland; ed. vibhuṅkṣyamāṇo]_aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].9) With <tvaṣṭā me []>, in the morning, about to distribute +[so Caland; ed. vibhuṅkṣyamāṇo], he eats
(KauśS_3,6[23].10) He ties a bowstring
(KauśS_3,6[23].11) Having wiped the staff with remainders, he holds it

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].12) <vāyur enāḥ [6.141]> iti yuktayoś citrākarma niśāyāṃ saṃbhārān saṃpātavataḥ karoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].12) With <vāyur enāḥ [6.141]>, at night, he performs the <s>citrākarma</s> (variegated/decorative rite) of the two yoked ones, making the ingredients with remainders

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].13) aparedyur <vāyur enāḥ [6.141]> iti śākhayā_udakadhārayā gāḥ parikrāmati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].13) On the following day, with <vāyur enāḥ [6.141]>, with a branch and a stream of water, he circumambulates the cows
(KauśS_3,6[23].14) Having placed a piece of the firstborn, with a knife of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree wood), <lohitena [6.141.2]> — as stated in the mantra

body.text: (KauśS_3,6[23].15) <yathā cakrur [6.141.3]> itīkṣukāśakāṇḍyā lohitaṃ nirmṛjya rasamiśram aśnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,6[23].15) With <yathā cakrur [6.141.3]>, having wiped off the blood with a stalk of sugarcane or <s>kāśa</s> (grass), he eats (it) mixed with <s>rasa</s> (juice)
(KauśS_3,6[23].16) Everything (should be) of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree wood)
(KauśS_3,6[23].17) With <yasyedam ā [6.33]> — this is the completion of the <s>āyojana</s> (yoking/harnessing) rites
(KauśS_3,7[24].1) With <uc chrayasva [6.142]> — the <s>bījopaharaṇa</s> (bringing/sowing of seeds)

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].2) ājyamiśrān yavān urvarāyāṃ kṛṣṭe phālena_uduhyānvṛcaṃ kāśīn ninayati nivapati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].2) Having ploughed barley grains mixed with ghee in the cultivated field with the ploughshare, he leads and scatters <s>kāśa</s> (grass) verse by verse

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].3) <abhi tyam [7.14]> iti mahāvakāśe_araṇya unnate vimite prāgdvārapratyagdvāreṣv apsu saṃpātān ānayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].3) With <abhi tyam [7.14]>, in a great open space, in the wilderness, on an elevated and measured ground, with doors facing east and west, he brings the remainders to the waters
(KauśS_3,7[24].4) On a black antelope skin, he gathers <s>Soma</s> shoots
(KauśS_3,7[24].5) He eats (the offering) with remainders, mixed with <s>Soma</s>
(KauśS_3,7[24].6) When kindled, it is accomplished
(KauśS_3,7[24].7) With <tāṃ savitaḥ [7.15]>, he ties the tether of a cow that has calved
(KauśS_3,7[24].8) With <saṃ mā siñcantu [7.33]>, mixed grains (are placed) in all waters
(KauśS_3,7[24].9) With <divyaṃ suparṇaṃ [7.39]>, with the staff-bearing bull's fat, he worships <s>Indra</s>
(KauśS_3,7[24].10) Having covered the cow-shed with the hide (of the animal) whose head and feet are still attached, he feeds <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with the prepared portions

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].11) proṣya samidha ādāya_ <ūrjaṃ bibhrad [7.60]> iti gṛhasaṃkāśe japati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].11) Having returned from abroad, having taken a fuel-stick, with <ūrjaṃ bibhrad [7.60]>, he recites when the house comes into sight

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].12) savyena samidho dakṣiṇena śālāvalīkaṃ saṃstabhya japati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].12) With the left (hand holding) fuel-sticks, with the right (hand) propping up the thatch of the hall, he recites

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].13) ativrajya samidha ādhāya <sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīme [so Caland; ed. susīme] _ahaṃ vāṃ gṛhapatir jīvyāsam> iti sthūṇe gṛhṇāty upatiṣṭhate
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].13) Having passed through, having placed the fuel-stick, with <sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīme [so Caland; ed. susīme] ahaṃ vāṃ gṛhapatir jīvyāsam> ('O auspicious one, rich in offspring, of good repose — may I, your householder, live long'), he grasps the two pillars and stands reverently
(KauśS_3,7[24].14) With <yad vadāmi [12.1.58]> — as stated in the mantra
(KauśS_3,7[24].15) Having sat down near the wife of the householder, he brings down a water vessel
(KauśS_3,7[24].16) With <ihaiva sta [7.60.7]>, when about to depart, he looks back
(KauśS_3,7[24].17) With <sūyavasād [7.73.11]>, he stations the animals in good pasture

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].18) dūrvāgrair añjalau_apa ānīya darśaṃ dārśībhir upatiṣṭhate
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].18) Having brought water in the cupped hands with tips of <s>dūrvā</s> (grass), he attends to the new-moon (rite) with the new-moon (verses)
(KauśS_3,7[24].19) With <indrasya kukṣir [7.111]> <sāhasras [9.4]>, he releases the bull with remainders

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].20) retodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi vayodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi yūthatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi gaṇatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi sahasrapoṣāyai tvātisṛjāmy aparimitapos.āyai tvātisṛjāmi
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].20) 'For the establishment of semen I release you; for the establishment of vitality I release you; for herd-formation I release you; for flock-formation I release you; for the nourishment of a thousand I release you; for unlimited nourishment I release you'

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].21) <etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ [9.4.24]> iti purāṇaṃ pravṛtya navam utsṛjate saṃprokṣati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].21) With <etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ [9.4.24]>, having turned away the old one, he releases the new one and sprinkles (it)
(KauśS_3,7[24].22) With the latter (hymn), one desiring prosperity worships <s>Indra</s> with a bull
(KauśS_3,7[24].23) One desiring success (worships) with a white (bull) on the full moon day
(KauśS_3,7[24].24) With <satyaṃ bṛhad [12.1]>, on the <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> (full moon of <s>Agrahāyaṇa</s>)
(KauśS_3,7[24].25) Behind the fire, on <s>darbha</s> (grasses), in a pit, a complete oblation
(KauśS_3,7[24].26) He eats the second (offering) with remainders

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].27) tṛtīyasyāditiḥ saptabhir <bhūme mātar [12.1.63]> iti trir juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].27) Of the third, <s>Aditi</s> (is the deity); with seven (verses) <bhūme mātar [12.1.63]> he offers three times

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].28) paścād agner darbheṣu kaśipu_āstīrya <vimṛgvarīṃ []> ity upaviśati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].28) Behind the fire, on <s>darbha</s> (grasses), having spread a cushion, with <vimṛgvarīṃ []> he sits down
(KauśS_3,7[24].29) With <yās te śivās [9.2.25]> he lies down
(KauśS_3,7[24].30) With <yac chayānaḥ []> he turns over

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].31) navabhiḥ <śantivā [12.1.59]> iti daśamyā_ <ud āyuṣā [3.31.10]> ity upottiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].31) With the nine (verses) <śantivā [12.1.59]>, and with the tenth <ud āyuṣā [3.31.10]>, he rises up
(KauśS_3,7[24].32) With <ud vayaṃ [7.53.7]> he steps out

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].33) <udīrāṇā [12.1.28]> iti trīṇi padāni prāṅ vā_udaṅ vā bāhyena_upaniṣkramya <yāvat te [12.1.33]> iti vīkṣate
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].33) With <udīrāṇā [12.1.28]>, having gone out three steps forward either eastward or northward, by the outer (path), with <yāvat te [12.1.33]> he looks around
(KauśS_3,7[24].34) And from an elevated place

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].35) purastād agneḥ sīraṃ yuktam udapātreṇa saṃpātavatāvasiñcati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].35) In front of the fire, he pours upon the yoked plough with a water vessel having remainders
(KauśS_3,7[24].36) This is the completion of the <s>āyojana</s> (yoking/harnessing) rites

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].37) <yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne [12.1.38-40]> iti juhoti varo ma āgamiṣyatīti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].37) With <yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne [12.1.38-40]> he offers, (thinking) 'May a bridegroom come to me'
(KauśS_3,7[24].38) With <yasyām annaṃ [12.1.42]> he stands reverently
(KauśS_3,7[24].39) With <nidhiṃ bibhrati [12.1.44-45]> — (he ties) an amulet, one desiring gold
(KauśS_3,7[24].40) Likewise, having found (treasure)
(KauśS_3,7[24].41) With <yasyāṃ kṛṣṇam [12.1.52]>, he sips (water) from what is produced by rain and brings it to the head

body.text: (KauśS_3,7[24].42) <yaṃ tvā pṛṣatī rathe [13.1.21-26]> iti dyauḥ pṛṣaty ādityo rohitaḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS_3,7[24].42) With <yaṃ tvā pṛṣatī rathe [13.1.21-26]> — <s>Dyaus</s> is the spotted (cow), <s>Āditya</s> is the red (bull)
(KauśS_3,7[24].43) He gives a spotted cow
(KauśS_3,7[24].44) With the milk of the spotted cow, a milk-rice oblation offered completely
(KauśS_3,7[24].45) This is the placing and attending of <s>puṣṭikarman</s> (prosperity rites)
(KauśS_3,7[24].46) With the water-hymns, (one attains) all desires; with the water-hymns, all desires

body.text: (KauśS 3 Colophon) iti atharvavede kauśikasūtre tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS 3 Colophon) Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Kauśikasūtra</s> in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>
(KauśS_4,1[25].1) Now, the <s>bhaiṣajya</s> (medical remedies/healing rites)

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].2) liṅgyupatāpo +bhiṣajyam [cf. Caland, AZ, p. 67, n.2 but also Speijer Museum 9 250]
body.translated_text: (KauśS_4,1[25].2) The medical treatment for one afflicted with <s>liṅga</s> (characteristic symptoms) and fever [cf. Caland, AZ, p. 67, n.2 but also Speijer Museum 9 250]
(KauśS_4,1[25].3) Other (treatments are known) from (specific) instruction
(KauśS_4,1[25].4) He anoints (the patient) with a water vessel having remainders, from the previous (rite)
(KauśS_4,1[25].5) He wipes away the wrinkles/marks

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].6) <vidmā śarasya [1.2.1]>_<ado yad [2.3.1 etc.]> iti muñjaśiro rajjvā badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS_4,1[25].6) With <vidmā śarasya [1.2.1]> <ado yad [2.3.1 etc.]>, he binds (the patient) with a <s>muñja</s> (grass) head-band and rope
(KauśS_4,1[25].7) Having scraped (earth from) a shaped clod and an anthill, he makes (the patient) drink (it)
(KauśS_4,1[25].8) He anoints (the patient) with clarified butter
(KauśS_4,1[25].9) He covers (the wound/patient)
(KauśS_4,1[25].10) With <vidmā śarasya [1.3.1]>, he ties the <s>pramehaṇa</s> (amulet against urinary disease)

(KauśS_4,1[25].11) He makes (the patient) drink (a decoction of) mouse(-dung), <s>kiri</s> (a plant), <s>pūtīka</s> (a plant), churned (curds), aged <s>pramanda</s> (a fermented drink), and <s>sāvraska</s> (another substance)
(KauśS_4,1[25].12) With the last two (verses), he makes (the patient) stand up
(KauśS_4,1[25].13) He makes (the patient) mount a vehicle
(KauśS_4,1[25].14) He releases an arrow
(KauśS_4,1[25].15) He loosens a bladder (poultice)
(KauśS_4,1[25].16) He splits/removes a wick (suppository)

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].17) ekaviṃśatiṃ yavān dohanyām adbhir ānīya drughnīṃ jaghane saṃstabhya phalato_avasiñcati
body.translated_text: (KauśS_4,1[25].17) Having brought twenty-one barley grains to the milking vessel with water, having propped up the <s>drughnī</s> (milch-cow) at the haunch, he pours (it) from the udder
(KauśS 4.1[25].18) He gives [the patient] a decoction (<s>phāṇṭa</s>) of <s>ālabi</s> (bottle-gourd) and <s>sola</s> (<s>Aeschynomene aspera</s>) to drink.
(KauśS 4.1[25].19) And for one who has upward-moving [disease] (<s>udāvartin</s>).
(KauśS 4.1[25].20) 'The waters go' [AV 1.4.1], 'Purified by <s>Vāyu</s>' — thus [are] the pacificatory [rites].
(KauśS 4.1[25].21) For the latter, [the rites are] accompanied by <s>Soma</s>.
(KauśS 4.1[25].22) Of the repelling [rites] — the procedure is explained by [their] expulsion.
(KauśS 4.1[25].23) He places [implements made of] tin, pestle, <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) wood, and <s>tārṣṭāgha</s> wood.

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].24) ayugmān khādirān_śaṅkūn <akṣyau ni vidhya [5.29.4]> iti paścād agneḥ samaṃbhūmi nihanti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.1[25].24) An odd number of <s>khadira</s> pegs — with [the verse] 'Piercing the two eyes' [AV 5.29.4] — he drives them behind the fire into the ground at ground level.
(KauśS 4.1[25].25) Likewise [pegs] of iron metal.
(KauśS 4.1[25].26) With heated pebbles he scatters [them around] the bedding — the heaps and folds.

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].27) amāvāsyāyāṃ sakṛdgṛhītān yavān anapahatān apratīhārapiṣṭān ābhicārikaṃ paristīrya tārṣṭāghedhma āvapati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.1[25].27) On the new-moon day, having spread as a sorcery [rite] barley grains that were grasped in a single handful, unhusked, ground without reverse-beating, he casts [them] with <s>tārṣṭāgha</s>-wood fuel.

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].28) ya āgachet taṃ brūyāt_śaṇaśulbena jihvāṃ nirmṛjānaḥ śālāyāḥ praskanda_iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.1[25].28) Whoever should come, he should tell him: 'Wipe your tongue with a hemp cord and jump away from the house.'
(KauśS 4.1[25].29) If he acts thus while not eating and denying [guilt] —
(KauśS 4.1[25].30) He offers <s>iṅgiḍa</s> (a kind of salt/mineral) mixed with <s>vīriṇa</s> (vetiver) fibres into a folded [leaf-cup].
(KauśS 4.1[25].31) He fastens the fuel and sacrificial grass in the house.
(KauśS 4.1[25].32) On the following day, when [things are] deformed, [the patient] suffers from [possession by] a <s>piśāca</s> (demon).
(KauśS 4.1[25].33) The oblation has been described [above].
(KauśS 4.1[25].34) Making the <s>añjali</s> (cupped-hands gesture) to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), reciting [the mantra], he gives [the patient water] to sip and sprinkles [him].
(KauśS 4.1[25].35) At night he drags [it] onto a firebrand.
(KauśS 4.1[25].36) He performs the auspicious opening rite (<s>svastyādya</s>).

body.text: (KauśS_4,1[25].37) <ayaṃ devānām [1.10.1]> iti_ekaviṃśatyā darbhapiñjūlībhir valīkaiḥ sārdham adhiśiro_avasiñcati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.1[25].37) 'This [is] of the gods' [AV 1.10.1] — with twenty-one <s>darbha</s>-grass brushes (<s>piñjūlī</s>), together with bark strips, he pours [water] over [the patient's] head.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].1) <jarāyujaḥ [1.12.1]> iti medo madhu sarpis tailaṃ pāyayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].1) 'Born from the afterbirth' [AV 1.12.1] — he gives fat, honey, ghee, and oil to drink.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].2) mauñjapraśnena śirasi_apihitaḥ savyena tita-uni pūlyāni dhārayamāṇo dakṣiṇenāvakiran vrajati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].2) With his head covered by a <s>muñja</s>-grass band, holding <s>tila</s> (sesame) seeds and clusters in his left [hand], scattering [them] with the right [hand], he goes forth.
(KauśS 4.2[26].3) In the left [hand], the <s>tila</s> and the band; in the right, the bowstring [and] the killing-club.
(KauśS 4.2[26].4) The command-giver [goes] in front.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].5) yatra_enaṃ vyādhir gṛhṇāti tatra tita-upraśnau nidadhāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].5) Where the disease seizes him, there he deposits the <s>tila</s> and the band.
(KauśS 4.2[26].6) And the bowstring.
(KauśS 4.2[26].7) The return journey.
(KauśS 4.2[26].8) Ghee [is administered] into the nostrils.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].9) pañcaparvaṇā lalāṭaṃ saṃstabhya japati_ <amūr yā [1.17.1]> iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].9) Pressing the forehead with a five-jointed [reed], he recites 'Those [stars] yonder' [AV 1.17.1].
(KauśS 4.2[26].10) With a five-jointed [reed] he scatters dust and sand around [the patient].
(KauśS 4.2[26].11) He ties on an <s>arma</s>-skull amulet.
(KauśS 4.2[26].12) He gives [it] to drink.
(KauśS 4.2[26].13) With four <s>dūrvā</s>-grass tips he gives curds mixed with sesame-cake to drink.
(KauśS 4.2[26].14) 'Following the sun' [AV 1.22.1] — he gives [the patient] a sipping [of water] mixed with the hair of the [animal] mentioned in the mantra.
(KauśS 4.2[26].15) And having brought [it] to the back.
(KauśS 4.2[26].16) He ties a <s>śaṅkudhāna</s> (peg-holder) amulet on [the patient] seated on a hide, with the milk-remainders (<s>saṃpāta</s>).
(KauśS 4.2[26].17) He gives [it] to drink.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].18) haridraudanabhuktam ucchiṣṭān ucchiṣṭenā prapadāt pralipya mantroktān adhastalpe haritasūtreṇa savyajaṅghāsu baddhvāvasnāpayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].18) Having eaten turmeric-rice, smearing from the leftover food, from the toes, [the substances] mentioned in the mantra, under the bed, having tied [them] on the left shanks with a green thread, he bathes [the patient].
(KauśS 4.2[26].19) He causes [the patient] to set forth.
(KauśS 4.2[26].20) He presents [the patient] to those who speak [auspiciously].
(KauśS 4.2[26].21) Having smeared breast-hairs with lac, having covered [them] with gold,

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].22) <naktaṃjātā [1.23.1]> <suparṇo jātaḥ [1.24.1]> iti mantroktaṃ śakṛdā(see Caland, Kl.Schr., p. 59)_ālohitaṃ praghṛṣyālimpati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].22) 'Born at night' [AV 1.23.1], 'The eagle is born' [AV 1.24.1] — he rubs the [substance] mentioned in the mantra, [namely] dung up to [the point of being] bloody, and anoints [the patient].
(KauśS 4.2[26].23) Having cut off grey hairs,
(KauśS 4.2[26].24) covered with wind-[blown substances],
(KauśS 4.2[26].25) 'If <s>Agni</s>' [AV 1.25.1] — reciting, he heats an axe, boils [a decoction], and pours [it over the patient].

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].26) <upa prāgād [1.28.1]> iti_udvijamānasya śuklaprasūnasya vīriṇasya catasṛṇām iṣīkāṇām ubhayataḥ pratyuṣṭaṃ badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].26) 'He approached' [AV 1.28.1] — for one who is frightened, [with] a white-blossomed <s>vīriṇa</s> (vetiver), he ties [an amulet] of four <s>iṣīkā</s> (rushes) scorched on both ends.
(KauśS 4.2[26].27) A triply-scorched reed-joint amulet.
(KauśS 4.2[26].28) The auspicious opening rite on a firebrand.
(KauśS 4.2[26].29) Named [after] the mother — having offered all fragrant powders anointed [with ghee], he smears [the patient] with the remainder.
(KauśS 4.2[26].30) And at a crossroads, on the head — in a <s>darbha</s>-grass tray, on an ember-potsherd, anointed [powders].
(KauśS 4.2[26].31) Wading against the current through <s>tila</s> (sesame) seeds, the other [person] shaves [the patient's hair] and pours [water] from behind.
(KauśS 4.2[26].32) Having poured [water] into a raw vessel, he ties [an amulet] on a <s>muñja</s>-grass tripod, an age-restoring [device].

(KauśS 4.2[26].33) [The verses are:] 'The one who hates evil' [AV 2.7.1], 'May the goddess be auspicious to us' [AV 2.25.1], '<s>Varaṇa</s>' [AV 6.85.1], '<s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper)' [AV 6.109.1], 'Of the abscess' [AV 6.127.1], 'Those that are brown' [AV 8.7.1] — thus.
(KauśS 4.2[26].34) With the penultimate [verse], he anoints [the patient] with a four-finger[-wide strip] of <s>palāśa</s> (<s>Butea monosperma</s>).
(KauśS 4.2[26].35) With the first [verse], he ties on the [substance] mentioned in the mantra.
(KauśS 4.2[26].36) With the second, he smears [the patient] with the remainder (<s>saṃpāta</s>) of the [substance] mentioned in the mantra.
(KauśS 4.2[26].37) With the third, he ties on the [substance] mentioned in the mantra.
(KauśS 4.2[26].38) With the fourth, he feeds [the patient].
(KauśS 4.2[26].39) With the fifth, he brings the remainders to the head of one seized by <s>Varuṇa</s> (i.e., afflicted with dropsy).
(KauśS 4.2[26].40) With the last [verse] — a potsherd [rite].
(KauśS 4.2[26].41) 'They went up' [AV 2.8.1] — he bathes [the patient] outside.
(KauśS 4.2[26].42) 'Drink this' [AV 2.8.2] — at dawn.

body.text: (KauśS_4,2[26].43) <babhror [2.8.3]> iti mantroktam ākṛtiloṣṭavalmīkau parilikhya jīvakoṣaṇyām utsīvya badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.2[26].43) 'Of the brown one' [AV 2.8.3] — having scratched [an image of] the [substance] mentioned in the mantra in a shaped clod and an anthill, having sifted out [the remedy] in warm water, he ties [it as an amulet].
(KauśS 4.3[27].1) 'Obeisance to your ploughshares' [AV 2.8.4] — he pours [water from] the yoke of a plough over [the patient's] head.
(KauśS 4.3[27].2) 'Obeisance to the one with flowing eyes' [AV 2.8.5] — in an empty house, he brings the remainders into the waters.
(KauśS 4.3[27].3) The latter [verse is performed] at an old, dug-out [place], together with the thatch of the house.
(KauśS 4.3[27].4) In that [water] he gives [the patient water] to sip and bathes [him].
(KauśS 4.3[27].5) 'Ten trees' [AV 2.9.1] — a potsherd [rite].
(KauśS 4.3[27].6) Ten friends, reciting, touch [the patient].

body.text: (KauśS_4,3[27].7) <kṣetriyāt tvā [2.10.1]>_iti catuṣpathe kāmpīlaśakalaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjūlībhir āplāvayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.3[27].7) 'From <s>kṣetriya</s> (hereditary disease), you' [AV 2.10.1] — at a crossroads, having tied <s>kāmpīla</s> (Rottleria tinctoria) chips at the joints, he bathes [the patient] with [grass] brushes.
(KauśS 4.3[27].8) He pours [water over the patient].
(KauśS 4.3[27].9) 'Of the earthly one' [AV 2.29.1] — at sunrise, he seats [two persons] back to back.

body.text: (KauśS_4,3[27].10) prāṅmukhaṃ vyādhitam pratyaṅmukham avyādhitaṃ śākhāsūpaveśya vaitase camase_upamanthanībhyāṃ tṛṣṇāgṛhītasya śirasi mantham upamathyātṛṣitāya prayachati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.3[27].10) Seating the diseased one facing east and the healthy one facing west on branches — in a <s>vaitasa</s> (rattan) cup, with churning-sticks, he churns a drink (<s>mantha</s>) on the head of one seized by thirst, and gives [it] to the unthirsty one.
(KauśS 4.3[27].11) In that [cup] he gathers the grasses.
(KauśS 4.3[27].12) He gives the drawn-up water to drink.
(KauśS 4.3[27].13) 'Clothed together' [AV 2.29.6c] — the [substance] mentioned in the mantra.

body.text: (KauśS_4,3[27].14) <indrasya yā mahī [2.31.1]>_iti khalvaṅgān alāṇḍūn hananān ghṛtamiśrān_juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.3[27].14) 'The great one of <s>Indra</s>' [AV 2.31.1] — he offers <s>khalvaṅga</s> (club-plant), <s>alāṇḍu</s> (a plant), and killing-[herbs] mixed with ghee.

body.text: (KauśS_4,3[27].15) bālān kalmāṣe kāṇḍe savyaṃ pariveṣṭya saṃbhinatti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.3[27].15) Having wound hairs around the left [side of] a spotted stalk, he splits [it].
(KauśS 4.3[27].16) He heats [it].
(KauśS 4.3[27].17) He places [it on the patient].
(KauśS 4.3[27].18) With the left [hand], facing south, having churned dust, he scatters [it] around.
(KauśS 4.3[27].19) He crushes [it].
(KauśS 4.3[27].20) He places [it on the patient].
(KauśS 4.3[27].21) 'The rising sun' [AV 2.32.1] — at sunrise, [he says] 'O cow by name,' thus — 'that one yonder,' thus.
(KauśS 4.3[27].22) At the end of the hymn — 'They are slain,' thus.
(KauśS 4.3[27].23) He casts [them away] with <s>darbha</s> grasses.
(KauśS 4.3[27].24) And at midday.
(KauśS 4.3[27].25) Toward the west, in the afternoon.
(KauśS 4.3[27].26) Having cut off a tuft of hair — the <s>khalva</s> and other [remedies].
(KauśS 4.3[27].27) 'From your two eyes' [AV 2.33.1] — a <s>vībarha</s> (a specific plant).
(KauśS 4.3[27].28) He pours [water] from a water-vessel with the remainders.
(KauśS 4.3[27].29) 'Of the deer' [AV 3.7.1] — with tying, giving to drink, sipping, peg-holder, and flame — when a [particular] asterism descends, he pours [water over the patient].
(KauśS 4.3[27].30) He casts in barley grains grasped in a single handful [into water] of unlimited measure.
(KauśS 4.3[27].31) He gives food.
(KauśS 4.3[27].32) 'I release you' [AV 3.11.1] — in the village, [with] rice [cooked with] stinking fish.
(KauśS 4.3[27].33) In the wilderness — with sesame, hemp, cow-dung, and pacificatory flame — when a [particular] asterism descends, he pours [water over the patient].
(KauśS 4.3[27].34) With [the exclamation] 'Release [him], O beast-companions!' — he bathes [the patient].

(KauśS 4.4[28].1) 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was born' [AV 4.6.1] — making the <s>añjali</s> (cupped-hands gesture) to <s>Takṣaka</s> (the serpent-king), reciting, he gives [the patient water] to sip and sprinkles [him].
(KauśS 4.4[28].2) Having ground a <s>kṛmuka</s>-shell fragment — with a <s>dūrśa</s>-grass, old deer-skin, and a piece [of each], with flame —

body.text: (KauśS_4,4[28].3) saṃpātavati_udapātre_ūrdhvaphalābhyāṃ digdhābhyāṃ mantham upamathya rayidhāraṇapiṇḍān anvṛcaṃ prakīrya chardayate
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.4[28].3) In a water-vessel with remainders, with the two [sticks] having the fruits facing upward, having churned a drink (<s>mantha</s>) with the two anointed [sticks], scattering the wealth-holding lumps verse by verse, he causes [the patient to] vomit.
(KauśS 4.4[28].4) He gives turmeric in ghee to drink.
(KauśS 4.4[28].5) 'O healing one' [AV 4.12.1] — when a [particular] asterism descends, he pours [water over the patient].
(KauśS 4.4[28].6) He gives <s>pṛṣātaka</s> (spotted [remedy]) to drink and anoints [the patient].
(KauśS 4.4[28].7) 'He sees' [AV 4.20.1] — he ties on an amulet of <s>sadaṃpuṣpa</s> (ever-blossoming [plant]).

body.text: (KauśS_4,4[28].8) <bhavāśarvau [4.28.1]>_iti sapta kāmpīlapuṭān apāṃ pūrṇān saṃpātavataḥ kṛtvā dakṣiṇenāvasicya paścād apavidhyati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.4[28].8) '<s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>' [AV 4.28.1] — having made seven <s>kāmpīla</s> leaf-cups filled with water and with remainders, pouring [water] to the right, he throws [them] away behind.
(KauśS 4.4[28].9) 'Filled by you' [AV 4.37.1] — with a cup, <s>śamī</s>-tree powder in food,
(KauśS 4.4[28].10) for adornment.
(KauśS 4.4[28].11) He encircles the house [with a cord].
(KauśS 4.4[28].12) 'And the immortal life-force' [AV 5.1.7] — he gives food to one seized by [loss of] understanding.
(KauśS 4.4[28].13) He anoints [the patient] with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus) marks mixed with butter, without reverse-wiping.
(KauśS 4.4[28].14) With lac marks — he gives decoctions (<s>phāṇṭa</s>) in milk to drink.
(KauśS 4.4[28].15) 'The <s>Brahman</s> was born' [AV 5.6.1] — he causes [the patient] to set forth [with the rites of] the lying-in woman and the <s>ariṣṭaka</s> (soapnut tree).
(KauśS 4.4[28].16) Churning, sipping, and worship of the sun (<s>Āditya</s>).

body.text: (KauśS_4,4[28].17) <dive svāhā [5.9.1]>_<imaṃ yavam [6.91.1]> iti catura udapātre saṃpātān ānayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.4[28].17) 'To heaven, <s>svāhā</s>' [AV 5.9.1], 'This barley' [AV 6.91.1] — he brings the four remainders into a water-vessel.
(KauśS 4.4[28].18) Two [remainders are placed] on the earth.
(KauśS 4.4[28].19) Having drawn those back, he bathes [the patient].
(KauśS 4.4[28].20) And with barley — with the latter [verse] he ties barley [as an amulet].
(KauśS 4.5[29].1) 'The giver indeed' [AV 5.13.1] — to <s>Takṣaka</s>; thus it has been stated.
(KauśS 4.5[29].2) With the second [verse] — the seizing [rite].
(KauśS 4.5[29].3) He walks around to the left.
(KauśS 4.5[29].4) He unties the knots in the pillars at the roof-ridge.
(KauśS 4.5[29].5) With the third [verse] — the driving-forth [rite].

body.text: (KauśS_4,5[29].6) caturthyā dakṣiṇam <apehy [7.88]>_iti daṃśma tṛṇaiḥ prakarṣyāhim abhinirasyati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.5[29].6) With the fourth, [going] to the right — 'Go away' [AV 7.88] — seizing the snake with grasses and tongs, he expels it,
(KauśS 4.5[29].7) from where [the patient] was bitten.
(KauśS 4.5[29].8) With the fifth [verse] — with bark-strips, sesame cake, and flame.
(KauśS 4.5[29].9) With the sixth — with a sinew-bowstring snare.
(KauśS 4.5[29].10) With two [verses] — he gives honey-libations to drink.
(KauśS 4.5[29].11) With the ninth — porcupine dung.
(KauśS 4.5[29].12) With the triply-white [verse] — he feeds [the patient] meat.
(KauśS 4.5[29].13) With the tenth — he gives a gourd [decoction] to sip.
(KauśS 4.5[29].14) With the eleventh — he ties [an amulet on] the navel.
(KauśS 4,5[29].15) Having pounded <s>khalatu</s>-leaf (<s>parṇī</s>) together with honey-plant and <s>vṛṣaliṅga</s>, he gives [it] to drink in a honey-mixture.
(KauśS 4,5[29].16) With the subsequent [verses], he eats.
(KauśS 4,5[29].17) He opens the door.
(KauśS 4,5[29].18) With [the hymn] '<s>agnis takmānam</s>' [AV 5.22.1], he gives parched grain to drink.
(KauśS 4,5[29].19) In a forest fire, he brings the remainders in a red vessel to [the patient's] head.
(KauśS 4,5[29].20) With [the hymn] '<s>ote me</s>' [AV 5.23.1], [he uses] the root of a <s>karīra</s> (caper) plant, [and] a portion [cut] with a stalk.
(KauśS 4,5[29].21) Dust from a village.

body.text: (KauśS_4,5[29].22) paścād agner mātur upasthe musalabudhnena navanītānvaktena triḥ pratīhāraṃ tālūni tāpayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,5[29].22) Behind the fire, in the mother's lap, with the bottom of a pestle smeared with fresh butter, he heats the palate three times with strokes.
(KauśS 4,5[29].23) He anoints with <s>śigru</s> (horseradish tree) [leaves] mixed with fresh butter.
(KauśS 4,5[29].24) Twenty-one <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver) [roots] — with [the verse] '<s>bhinadmi</s>' [AV 5.23.13c], as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4,5[29].25) He presents the <s>uśīra</s> [roots].
(KauśS 4,5[29].26) Together with the twenty-one [roots], he bathes [the patient].
(KauśS 4,5[29].27) With [the hymn] '<s>ā yaṃ viśanti</s>' [AV 6.2.2], he eats milk-rice cooked with [the material from] a bird's nest.
(KauśS 4,5[29].28) With [the hymn] '<s>pari dyām iva</s>' [AV 6.12.1], he gives [the patient] honey-drink to drink.
(KauśS 4,5[29].29) While reciting.
(KauśS 4,5[29].30) With [the hymn] '<s>asthisraṃsam</s>' [AV 6.14.1], having offered a chip in the waters with the remainder, he pours over [the patient].
(KauśS 4,6[30].1) With [the hymn] '<s>ābayaḥ</s>' [AV 6.16.1], he ties on mustard [seeds] with the remainder of oil.
(KauśS 4,6[30].2) Having smeared a stalk,
(KauśS 4,6[30].3) he presents mixed vegetables.
(KauśS 4,6[30].4) He presents four vegetable-fruits.
(KauśS 4,6[30].5) He anoints [the patient] with a milk-confection.
(KauśS 4,6[30].6) He eats.
(KauśS 4,6[30].7) With [the hymn] '<s>agner iva</s>' [AV 6.20.1] — the said [rite is performed] in a forest fire.
(KauśS 4,6[30].8) With [the hymn] '<s>imā yas tisraḥ</s>' [AV 6.21.1], at the base of a tree, he pours over [the patient] with [water heated by] a born flame.
(KauśS 4,6[30].9) With [fragments from] the skull, bones, and eyes.
(KauśS 4,6[30].10) With two [types of] <s>nikaṭa</s> [plant materials].
(KauśS 4,6[30].11) With [the hymn] '<s>kṛṣṇaṃ niyānam</s>' [AV 6.22.1], he sprinkles with herbs.
(KauśS 4,6[30].12) The conclusion of the wind [disease] rites.

body.text: (KauśS_4,6[30].13) <himavataḥ [6.24.1]>_iti +syandamānā [ed.: syandamānād; Caland, Kl. Schr., p. 59] anvīpam āhārya valīkaiḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,6[30].13) With [the hymn] '<s>himavataḥ</s>' [AV 6.24.1], having brought [water] flowing along the bank, with bark pieces,

body.text: (KauśS_4,6[30].14) <pañca ca yā [6.25.1]>_iti pañca pañcāśataṃ paraśuparṇān kāṣṭhair ādīpayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,6[30].14) with [the hymn] '<s>pañca ca yāḥ</s>' [AV 6.25.1], he kindles fifty-five <s>paraśuparṇa</s> (axe-leaf) [herbs] with pieces of wood.
(KauśS 4,6[30].15) He smears a measured amount in a skull-cup with a piece of wood.
(KauśS 4,6[30].16) He causes [the patient] to be bitten by lice, flies, <s>jāmbīla</s> [insects], water-spiders, mosquitoes, and the like.
(KauśS 4,6[30].17) At night, with [the hymn] '<s>ava mā pāpman</s>' [AV 6.26.1], having poured out <s>tita</s> (parched grain) bundles and having discarded [them],
(KauśS 4,6[30].18) the following day, having thrown three cake-balls as offerings to the thousand-eyed one [<s>Indra</s>] into the waters at a crossroads, he scatters [them].

(KauśS 4,7[31].1) With [the hymn] '<s>yas te madaḥ</s>' [AV 6.30.2], having produced [fire] with a <s>śamī</s> (Prosopis) [wood] with <s>śamī</s>-and-<s>śamyāka</s> [sticks], for one marked by shaved head and evil signs, he shaves.
(KauśS 4,7[31].2) [Shaving] over the head.

body.text: (KauśS_4,7[31].3) <antardāve [6.32.1]>_iti samantam agneḥ karṣvām uṣṇapūrṇāyāṃ japan_triḥ parikramya puroḍāśaṃ juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,7[31].3) With [the hymn] '<s>antardāve</s>' [AV 6.32.1], having gone around the fire three times while reciting, on all sides, in a furrow filled with hot [ashes], he offers a sacrificial cake.
(KauśS 4,7[31].4) With [the hymns] '<s>prāgnaye</s>' [AV 6.34.1], '<s>pretaḥ</s>' [AV 7.114.2], he should place [the offering].
(KauśS 4,7[31].5) With the two <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [hymns], the drink-offerings.

body.text: (KauśS_4,7[31].6) <asthād dyaur [6.44.1/6.77.1(?)]> ity apavātāyāḥ svayaṃsrastena gośṛṅgeṇa saṃpātavatā japan
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,7[31].6) With [the hymn] '<s>asthād dyauḥ</s>' [AV 6.44.1/6.77.1(?)], for a woman who has had a miscarriage, reciting while [using] a naturally-fallen cow's horn with the remainder,
(KauśS 4,7[31].7) with [the hymn] '<s>yāṃ te Rudra</s>' [AV 6.90.1], [he gives] a trident to one bearing a trident.
(KauśS 4,7[31].8) With [the hymn] '<s>ut sūryaḥ</s>' [AV 6.52.1], [he uses] <s>śamī</s> fruit, <s>bimba</s> (Coccinia), and <s>śīrṇaparṇī</s> (dried-leaf plant).
(KauśS 4,7[31].9) With [the hymn] '<s>dyauś ca me</s>' [AV 6.53.1], having anointed, he wipes off.
(KauśS 4,7[31].10) He draws down along a post.
(KauśS 4,7[31].11) With [the hymn] '<s>idam id vā</s>' [AV 6.57.1], having sprinkled unbroken grain with the foam of urine,
(KauśS 4,7[31].12) he throws in.
(KauśS 4,7[31].13) He washes.
(KauśS 4,7[31].14) He smears with tooth-dust.
(KauśS 4,7[31].15) With dust of a grass-tuft.
(KauśS 4,7[31].16) With [the hymns] '<s>apacitaḥ</s>' [AV 6.83.1], '<s>ā susrasaḥ</s>' [AV 7.76.1], [the rites for] lice and the like.
(KauśS 4,7[31].17) Having pounded red salt, he spits on [the affected area].
(KauśS 4,7[31].18) With [the hymn] '<s>antarikṣeṇa</s>' [AV 6.80.1], [for one] struck on the flank — as stated in the <s>mantra</s>, walking about.
(KauśS 4,7[31].19) He fumigates with an insect.
(KauśS 4,7[31].20) With [the verse] '<s>glauḥ</s>' [AV 6.83.3c], with unbroken grain.

body.text: (KauśS_4,7[31].21) <vīhi svām [6.83.4]> ity ajñātāruḥ śāntyudakena saṃprokṣya manasā saṃpātavatā
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,7[31].21) With [the verse] '<s>vīhi svām</s>' [AV 6.83.4], one who has climbed an unknown [tree], having sprinkled with pacificatory water, mentally, with the remainder,
(KauśS 4,7[31].22) with [the hymn] '<s>yā oṣadhayaḥ</s>' [AV 6.96.1], he fumigates with the herbs mentioned in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4,7[31].23) He gives a honey-and-<s>daśvit</s> (ten-fold) mixture to drink.
(KauśS 4,7[31].24) A milk-and-<s>daśvit</s> mixture.
(KauśS 4,7[31].25) And both [combined].
(KauśS 4,7[31].26) With [the hymn] '<s>devā aduḥ</s>' [AV 6.100.1], with anthill [material] — binding, giving to drink, sipping, and anointing — with hot [water].
(KauśS 4,7[31].27) With [the hymns] '<s>yathā manaḥ</s>' [AV 6.105.1], '<s>ava divaḥ</s>' [AV 7.107.1], with <s>ariṣṭa</s> (soap-nut) [tree materials].

body.text: (KauśS_4,7[31].28) <devī devyām [6.136.1]>_<yāṃ jamadagnir [6.137.1]> iti mantroktāphalaṃ jīvyalākābhyām amāvāsyāyāṃ kṛṣṇavasanaḥ kṛṣṇabhakṣaḥ purā kākasaṃpātād avanakṣatre_avasiñcati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,7[31].28) With [the hymns] '<s>devī devyām</s>' [AV 6.136.1], '<s>yāṃ Jamadagniḥ</s>' [AV 6.137.1], the fruit mentioned in the <s>mantra</s> — with lac and lacquer, on the new-moon night, wearing black clothing, eating black food, before the alighting of crows, under the <s>ava</s> constellation — he pours over.
(KauśS 4,8[32].1) With [the hymn] '<s>yas te stanaḥ</s>' [AV 7.10.1], for one seized by <s>jambha</s> (jaw-disease), he presents the breast.
(KauśS 4,8[32].2) He gives to drink <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) grains milked upon [them].

body.text: (KauśS_4,8[32].3) <agnāviṣṇū [7.29.1]> <somārudrā [7.42.1]> <sinīvāli [7.46.1]> <vi te muñcāmi [7.78.1]> <śumbhanī [7.112.1]> iti mauñjaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjulībhir āplāvayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,8[32].3) With [the hymns] '<s>Agnāviṣṇū</s>' [AV 7.29.1], '<s>Somārudrā</s>' [AV 7.42.1], '<s>Sinīvālī</s>' [AV 7.46.1], '<s>vi te muñcāmi</s>' [AV 7.78.1], '<s>śumbhanī</s>' [AV 7.112.1], having bound [the patient] with <s>muñja</s>-grass [cords] at the joints, he bathes [them] with <s>piñjūlī</s> (broom-sticks).
(KauśS 4,8[32].4) He pours over.
(KauśS 4,8[32].5) With [the hymn] '<s>tiraścirājeḥ</s>' [AV 7.56.1], as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4,8[32].6) Having scratched around a figure, a clod of earth, and an anthill,
(KauśS 4,8[32].7) the drink-offerings.

body.text: (KauśS_4,8[32].8) <apacitāṃ [7.74.1]>_iti vaiṇavena dārbhyūṣeṇa kṛṣṇorṇājyena kālabundai stukāgrair iti mantroktam
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,8[32].8) With [the hymn] '<s>apacitām</s>' [AV 7.74.1], with a bamboo [instrument], with a <s>darbha</s>-grass powder, with black-wool ghee, with <s>kālabunda</s> [berry], with tuft-tips — as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4,8[32].9) On the fourth [day], having placed [the instrument] upon [the growth], he pierces.
(KauśS 4,8[32].10) With a bowstring-tuft flame.
(KauśS 4,8[32].11) With [the verse] '<s>yaḥ kīkasāḥ</s>' [AV 7.76.3], he ties a string of a <s>piśīla</s> (thin) <s>vīṇā</s> (lute).
(KauśS 4,8[32].12) With the string, an earthen [pot].
(KauśS 4,8[32].13) Having folded a <s>vīriṇa</s> (andropogon) leather strap, self-withered, three times,

body.text: (KauśS_4,8[32].14) <apsu te [7.83.1]>_iti vahantyor madhye vimite piñjūlībhir āplāvayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,8[32].14) with [the hymn] '<s>apsu te</s>' [AV 7.83.1], in the middle of two flowing [streams], at [their] confluence, he bathes [the patient] with <s>piñjūlī</s> (broom-sticks).
(KauśS 4,8[32].15) He pours over.
(KauśS 4,8[32].16) Hot [waters] with the remainder, [others] without the remainder.

body.text: (KauśS_4,8[32].17) <namo rūrāya [7.116.1]>_iti śakunīniveṣīkāñjimaṇḍūkaṃ nīlalohitābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ sakakṣaṃ baddhvā
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,8[32].17) With [the hymn] '<s>namo rūrāya</s>' [AV 7.116.1], having bound a bird, a <s>niveṣīkā</s> (reed), a <s>jimaṇḍūka</s> (frog) with blue and red threads, together with a tuft,
(KauśS 4,8[32].18) with [the hymn] '<s>śīrṣaktim</s>' [AV 9.8.1], he touches [the patient].
(KauśS 4,8[32].19) With the last two [verses], he worships the sun.
(KauśS 4,8[32].20) With [the hymn] '<s>Indrasya prathamaḥ</s>' [AV 10.4.1], for <s>Takṣaka</s> — as stated [previously].
(KauśS 4,8[32].21) Having drawn out the <s>paidva</s> [substance], with the right thumb into the right nostril,
(KauśS 4,8[32].22) in case of snake-fear, he hides [the patient] in a furrow.
(KauśS 4,8[32].23) With [the verse] '<s>aṅgād aṅgāt</s>' [AV 10.4.25], from the feet downward.
(KauśS 4,8[32].24) With the last verse of the bite [hymn], having tied [a ligature], he draws out the snake.
(KauśS 4,8[32].25) From where [the patient was] bitten.
(KauśS 4,8[32].26) [All uses of] herbs and trees that are recited upon and not prohibited [are valid] for medicinal purposes.
(KauśS 4,8[32].27) With verses having inauspicious signs.
(KauśS 4,8[32].28) Of the preceding [rite], for one desiring a son or one who has lost offspring, at the water's edge, with pacificatory [materials], over the head, he pours over.
(KauśS 4,8[32].29) For a woman who has returned [from the husband's house], he presents a sacrificial cake, mixed food, and ornaments, with the remainder.

body.text: (KauśS_4,9[33].1) <vaṣaṭ te pūṣann [1.11.1]> iti catura udapātre saṃpātān ānīya caturo muñjān mūrdhni vibṛhati prācaḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,9[33].1) With [the hymn] '<s>vaṣaṭ te Pūṣan</s>' [AV 1.11.1], having brought the remainders into four water vessels, he pulls out four <s>muñja</s> [grasses] from the top of the head, [placing them] eastward.
(KauśS 4,9[33].2) <s>Iṣīkā</s> (reed) stalks westward.
(KauśS 4,9[33].3) When they are being cut, [there is] uncertainty.
(KauśS 4,9[33].4) He bathes [the patient] with hot [water] from the right tuft of hair.
(KauśS 4,9[33].5) He unties the knots of the <s>śālā</s> (hall) [roof beams].
(KauśS 4,9[33].6) He ties a yoke-strap with a noose on both ends.

body.text: (KauśS_4,9[33].7) <yadi somasyāsi rājñaḥ somāt tvā rājño 'dhikrīṇāmi yadi varuṇasyāsi rājño varuṇāt tvā rājño 'dhikrīṇāmi [cf. GobhGS 2.6.6>_ity ekaviṃśatyā yavaiḥ srajaṃ parikirati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,9[33].7) [Saying:] 'If you belong to King <s>Soma</s>, I buy you from King <s>Soma</s>. If you belong to King <s>Varuṇa</s>, I buy you from King <s>Varuṇa</s>' [cf. GobhGS 2.6.6] — he scatters a garland with twenty-one barley grains.

body.text: (KauśS_4,9[33].8) <anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata sadhrīcīḥ savratā bhūtvāsyā avata vīryam [PS 1.65.4]> iti saṃnayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,9[33].8) With [the verse] 'Let one of you protect the other; let one attend upon the other; being united, of one vow, protect the potency of this one' [PS 1.65.4], he leads [the bride].

body.text: (KauśS_4,9[33].9) <mā te riṣan khanitā yasmai ca tvā khanāmasi | dvipāc catuṣpād asmākaṃ mā riṣad devy oṣadhe || [PS 1.65.3]> <srajo nāmāsi> <prajāpatiṣ ṭvām akhanad ātmane śalyasraṃsanam | tāṃ tvā vayaṃ khanāmasy amuṣmai tvā śalyasraṃsanam [-]> ity astamite chattreṇa vāntardhāya [ed. cāntar-, see Caland, Kl. Schr. p. 70] phālena khanati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,9[33].9) With [the verses] 'May the digger not harm you, nor he for whom we dig you; may neither two-footed nor four-footed of ours be harmed, O divine herb' [PS 1.65.3]; 'You are called a garland'; '<s>Prajāpati</s> dug you up for himself as an arrow-remover; we dig you up for so-and-so as an arrow-remover' — having concealed [himself] with an umbrella at sunset, he digs with a ploughshare.
(KauśS 4,9[33].10) With [the formula] 'May it succeed for you here,' he places the tip [of the herb].
(KauśS 4,9[33].11) With [the formula] 'Here for me,' he takes up the root.
(KauśS 4,9[33].12) [The herb should be found] in a single pond, unlicked [by animals] — [then] a male child [will be born].
(KauśS 4,9[33].13) Having wrapped [the herb] with <s>darbha</s> grass, he applies it to the hair.
(KauśS 4,9[33].14) Likewise for the <s>vibṛha</s> herb and the <s>śāka-vṛṣa</s> (vegetable-rain) [rite].
(KauśS 4,9[33].15) When the afterbirth has fallen, they lift [it] up.
(KauśS 4,9[33].16) The digging of herbs with a garland has been explained.
(KauśS 4,9[33].17) He drips water onto four <s>umā</s> (flax) fruits in the hand.
(KauśS 4,9[33].18) When [the fruits] roll together, [it indicates] a male child.
(KauśS 4,9[33].19) A descendant of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> touches the limbs [of the child].
(KauśS 4,9[33].20) [If the child bears] a masculine name, [it will be] a male child.

(KauśS 4,10[34].1) With [the hymn] '<s>idaṃ janāsaḥ</s>' [AV 1.32.1], for her, on <s>śiṃśapā</s> (dalbergia) branches, at the water's edge, with pacificatory [materials], over the head, he pours over.
(KauśS 4,10[34].2) For the woman who has returned [from the husband's house].

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].3) <nissālām [2.14.1]> ity avatokāyai kṛṣṇavasanāyai triṣu vimiteṣu prāgdvārapratyagdvāreṣu_apsu saṃpātān ānayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,10[34].3) With [the hymn] '<s>nissālām</s>' [AV 2.14.1], for a woman who has lost offspring, wearing black clothing — in three measured [places] with east-facing doors and west-facing doors — he brings the remainders into the waters.
(KauśS 4,10[34].4) The subsequent [remainders] on a <s>palāśa</s> (butea) leaf [and] on lead [pieces].
(KauśS 4,10[34].5) Having made [her] stand upon the lead [pieces], he bathes [her].
(KauśS 4,10[34].6) Having laid down [the materials], wearing black, she departs.
(KauśS 4,10[34].7) Having kindled [the fire], the <s>brahman</s> [priest acts].
(KauśS 4,10[34].8) Likewise for the first two [rites], the materials [are gathered] separately.
(KauśS 4,10[34].9) [This is] the branch-hymn.

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].10) paścād agner abhitaḥ kāṇḍe iṣīke nidhāyādhyadhi dhāyine audumbarīr ādhāpayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4,10[34].10) Behind the fire, on both sides, having placed the stalks and reeds, he has [the woman] set <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood) [fuel-sticks] on top, layer upon layer, for the nursing one.
(KauśS 4,10[34].11) For the woman who has most recently returned [from the husband's house], with the last [verse].
(KauśS 4,10[34].12) The rites for finding a husband.
(KauśS 4,10[34].13) With [the hymn] '<s>ā no Agne</s>' [AV 2.36.1], he feeds [her] <s>kṛśara</s> (rice-and-sesame porridge) [prepared as a charm for] the coming [of a husband].

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].14) mṛgākharād vedyāṃ mantroktāni saṃpātavanti dvāre prayachati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.10[34].14) From an animal burrow, on the altar (<s>vedī</s>), [he places] the items mentioned in the <s>mantras</s>, with remnants, and gives [them] at the door.

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].15) udakaṃse vrīhiyavau jāmyai niśi hutvā dakṣiṇena prakrāmati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.10[34].15) In a water-vessel, [he places] rice and barley; for the sister, at night, having offered, he departs by the right [side].

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].16) paścād agneḥ prakṣālya saṃdhāvya saṃpātavatīṃ <bhagasya nāvam [2.36.5]> iti mantroktam
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.10[34].16) Behind the fire, having washed and rubbed [them], with remnants — with '<s>bhagasya nāvam</s>' [AV 2.36.5], as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].17) saptadāmnyāṃ saṃpātavatyāṃ vatsān pratyantān +pracṛtantī +vahati [ed.: pracṛtanto vahanti; Caland, AZ, p. 113, n. 11]
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.10[34].17) With a seven-stranded [rope], with remnants, she leads the calves facing toward [her].
(KauśS 4.10[34].18) With a fresh [garment] with remnants, she touches the bull.
(KauśS 4.10[34].19) She makes [the bull] bellow toward whichever direction [she desires].
(KauśS 4.10[34].20) For the sister — with '<s>pra yad ete</s>' [AV 5.1.4], [she prepares] a mixture of rice and sesame for the arriving [guest].
(KauśS 4.10[34].21) With '<s>imā brahma</s>' [AV 5.2.8], for the female friend.

body.text: (KauśS_4,10[34].22) <ayam ā yāty [6.60.1]>_iti purā kākasaṃpātād aryamṇe juhoti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.10[34].22) With '<s>ayam ā yāty</s>' [AV 6.60.1], before the fall of the crow [i.e., before dawn], he offers to <s>Aryaman</s>.
(KauśS 4.10[34].23) At the inner door-posts, they carry the <s>bali</s> (offerings).
(KauśS 4.10[34].24) From whichever [direction] they approach.
(KauśS 4.11[35].1) Rites for procuring a male child (<s>puṃsavana</s>).
(KauśS 4.11[35].2) For a woman whose menstrual period has passed, [the rite is performed] under a male <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion).

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].3) <yena vehad [3.23.1]> iti bāṇaṃ mūrdhni vibṛhati badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].3) With '<s>yena vehad</s>' [AV 3.23.1], he pulls out an arrow [from the quiver] at the top of the head and ties it on.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].4) phālacamase sarūpavatsāyā dudghe vrīhiyavau_avadhāya mūrchayitvādhyaṇḍe bṛhatīpalāśavidaryau vā pratinīya paidvam iva
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].4) In a ploughshare-cup, having poured rice and barley into [milk] drawn from a cow with a calf of the same color, having curdled [it], with <s>bṛhatī</s> and <s>palāśa</s> leaves, or <s>vidarī</s> — having strained [it] as though [pouring] <s>paidva</s> milk.
(KauśS 4.11[35].5) With '<s>parvatād divo</s>' [AV 5.25.1], he feeds [the woman] a mixture of rice and sesame for the arriving [guest].
(KauśS 4.11[35].6) A second [portion is prepared] with a yoke-bar, with remnants.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].7) khe lūnān_ca palāśatsarūn nivṛtte nighṛṣyādhāya śiśne grāmaṃ praviśati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].7) Having cut <s>palāśa</s> shoots in the open [space], having rubbed [them] upon returning, having placed [them] on the penis, he enters the village.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].8) <śamīm aśvattha [6.11.1]> iti mantrokte_agniṃ mathitvā puṃsyāḥ sarpiṣi paidvam iva
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].8) With '<s>śamīm aśvattha</s>' [AV 6.11.1], as stated in the <s>mantra</s> — having churned fire, in clarified butter of a she-[animal], like <s>paidva</s> [milk].
(KauśS 4.11[35].9) He makes [the woman] drink a honey-drink (<s>madhumantha</s>).
(KauśS 4.11[35].10) Having wrapped with black wool threads, he ties [it] on.
(KauśS 4.11[35].11) With '<s>yantāsi</s>' [AV 6.80.2], he ties on as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].12) <ṛdhaṅmantro [5.1.1]>_ity ekā <yatheyaṃ pṛthivī [6.17.1-4]>_<acyutā [cf. sakalapāṭha-mantras at KauśS 98.2, AVPariś 11.1.11]>_iti garbhadṛṃhaṇāni
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].12) With '<s>ṛdhaṅmantro</s>' [AV 5.1.1] — [this is] one [group]; '<s>yatheyaṃ pṛthivī</s>' [AV 6.17.1-4], '<s>acyutā</s>' — these are the embryo-strengthening (<s>garbhadṛṃhaṇa</s>) [rites].

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].13) jambhagṛhītāya prathamāvarjaṃ jyāṃ trir udgrathya badhnāti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].13) For one seized by convulsions (<s>jambha</s>), having untwisted the bowstring three times with the first turn, he ties it on.
(KauśS 4.11[35].14) He makes [the patient] swallow clay lumps, verse by verse.
(KauśS 4.11[35].15) He scatters dark sand around the bed.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].16) yām iched vīraṃ janayed iti +dhātṛvyābhir (ed.: dhātar-; cf. Caland, Kl. Schr., p. 60) udaram abhimantrayate
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].16) [With the verse] 'If she desires that she bear a hero' — he consecrates the belly with <s>Dhātṛ</s>-[mantras].
(KauśS 4.11[35].17) With '<s>prajāpatir</s>' [AV 6.11.3/7.19.1], he offers into the lap of a woman desiring offspring.
(KauśS 4.11[35].18) He feeds [her] pieces of the flesh of a red she-goat.
(KauśS 4.11[35].19) [Given at] the end-portions.
(KauśS 4.11[35].20) With '<s>yau te mātā</s>' [AV 8.6.1], he ties on as stated in the <s>mantras</s>.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].21) <yathedaṃ bhūmyā adhi [2.30.1]> <yathā vṛkṣaṃ [6.8.1]> <+vāñcha me [6.9.1]> <yathāyaṃ vāho [6.102.1]>_iti saṃspṛṣṭayor vṛkṣalibujayoḥ śakalāvantareṣusthakarāñjanakuṣṭhamadughareṣmamathitatṛṇam ājyena saṃnīya saṃspṛśati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].21) With '<s>yathedaṃ bhūmyā adhi</s>' [AV 2.30.1], '<s>yathā vṛkṣaṃ</s>' [AV 6.8.1], '<s>vāñcha me</s>' [AV 6.9.1], '<s>yathāyaṃ vāho</s>' [AV 6.102.1] — having mixed splints from two trees touching [each other], together with antimony (<s>añjana</s>), <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>madughā</s>, <s>reṣma</s>, and churned grass, with clarified butter — he touches [the woman].
(KauśS 4.11[35].22) With '<s>uttudas tvā</s>' [AV 3.25.1], he pushes with a finger.
(KauśS 4.11[35].23) He places twenty-one [sticks] with thorns facing east, adorned, recited over.
(KauśS 4.11[35].24) [He takes them] from the tips of a winnowing basket, with strings attached.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].25) navanītānvaktaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ trir ahnaḥ pratapati trirātre
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].25) <s>Kuṣṭha</s> [plant] anointed with fresh butter — he heats [it] three times a day for three nights.
(KauśS 4.11[35].26) Having immersed [oneself] in long lotuses, one lies down.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].27) uṣṇodakaṃ tripāde pattaḥ +prabadhya_(ed.: prabaddhā; Bloomfield, SBE 42, p. 358, n. 3]_aṅguṣṭhābhyām ardayan_śete (ed. misprint: ardayañ chate; see Caland, Kl. Schr., p. 51)
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].27) With warm water in a three-legged [vessel], having bound [his feet] while seated, pressing with the thumbs, he lies down.

body.text: (KauśS_4,11[35].28) pratikṛtim āvalekhanīṃ dārbhyūṣeṇa bhāṅgajyena kaṇṭakaśalyayā_ulūkapattrayāsitālakāṇḍayā hṛdaye vidhyati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.11[35].28) He pierces an image [made for] scratching in the heart with a <s>darbha</s>-grass needle, a hemp string, a thorn-lancet, owl-feather, and a stalk of black <s>ālaka</s>.
(KauśS 4.12[36].1) With '<s>sahasraśṛṅgo</s>' [AV 4.5.1] — [this is] a sleep-inducing charm (<s>svāpana</s>).

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].2) udapātreṇa saṃpātavatā śālāṃ saṃprokṣyāparasmin dvārapakṣe nyubjati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].2) Having sprinkled the house with a water-vessel with remnants, he places [it] upside down at the further door-post.
(KauśS 4.12[36].3) Likewise, [he does this] naked.

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].4) ulūkhalam uttarāṃ sraktiṃ dakṣiṇaśayanapādaṃ tantūn abhimantrayate
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].4) [He consecrates] a mortar, the northern door-post, the foot of the southern bed[-side], and threads.
(KauśS 4.12[36].5) With '<s>asthād dyaur</s>' [AV 6.77.1/6.44.1] — [this is] a binding charm (<s>niveṣṭana</s>).
(KauśS 4.12[36].6) Having tied the top of a bamboo with a binding, he ties [it] at the middle [post].
(KauśS 4.12[36].7) And at the bed-foot and in [a vessel of] lotuses.
(KauśS 4.12[36].8) And having drawn [one toward the other].
(KauśS 4.12[36].9) With the drawing [instrument], he offers sesame.
(KauśS 4.12[36].10) With '<s>idaṃ yat preṇyaḥ</s>' [AV 6.89.1], he consecrates the head and ear.
(KauśS 4.12[36].11) He holds the hair.

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].12) <bhagena mā [6.129.1]> <nyastikā [6.139.1]>_<idaṃ khanāmi [7.38.1]>_iti sauvarcalam oṣadhivat_śuklaprasūnaṃ śirasi_upacṛtya grāmaṃ praviśati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].12) With '<s>bhagena mā</s>' [AV 6.129.1], '<s>nyastikā</s>' [AV 6.139.1], '<s>idaṃ khanāmi</s>' [AV 7.38.1] — having applied <s>sauvarcala</s> salt like a herb, and a white flower, on the head — he enters the village.
(KauśS 4.12[36].13) With '<s>rathajitāṃ</s>' [AV 6.130.1], he scatters love-charm beans.
(KauśS 4.12[36].14) He hurls blazing reed-arrows in each direction — the scratching [implements] facing toward [him].

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].15) <bhagam asyā varca [1.14.1]> iti mālāniṣpramandadantadhāvanakeśamīśānahatāyā anustaraṇyā vā kośam ulūkhaladaraṇe triśile nikhanati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].15) With '<s>bhagam asyā varca</s>' [AV 1.14.1] — [he takes] a garland, a <s>niṣpramanda</s> [tooth-stick], a tooth-brush, and hair of [a woman] slain by <s>Īśāna</s>, or a spreading [hide] — [and] buries [them] in a shell in a mortar-groove, at a crossroads.
(KauśS 4.12[36].16) Having churned the garland, he recites.

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].17) trīṇi keśamaṇḍalāni kṛṣṇasūtrena vigrathya triśile_aśmottarāṇi vyatyāsam
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].17) Having twisted three hair-rings with a black thread, at a crossroads, [he places them] on stones, in alternating order.

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].18) athāsyai bhagam utkhanati <yaṃ te bhagaṃ nicakhnus triśile yaṃ catuḥśile | idaṃ tam utkhanāmi prajayā ca dhanena ca [-]>_iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].18) Then he digs up her sexual organ [symbolically], [reciting]: 'That sexual organ of yours which they buried at a crossroads, at a trident[-intersection], or at a four-way [intersection] — this I dig up, with offspring and with wealth.'

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].19) <imāṃ khanāmy [3.18.1]>_iti bāṇāparṇīṃ lohitājāyā drapsena saṃnīya śayanam anuparikirati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].19) With '<s>imāṃ khanāmy</s>' [AV 3.18.1], having mixed <s>bāṇāparṇī</s> [plant] with a drop [of blood] of a red she-goat, he scatters [it] around the bed.
(KauśS 4.12[36].20) With '<s>abhi te 'dhāṃ</s>' [AV 3.18.6a], he applies a <s>palāśa</s> [leaf] from below.
(KauśS 4.12[36].21) With '<s>upa te 'dhāṃ</s>' [AV 3.18.6b], he places [one] above.
(KauśS 4.12[36].22) When about to lead [the woman] willingly, going against the sun, scattering uncounted pebbles, he proceeds.
(KauśS 4.12[36].23) While crushing, he mutters [the <s>mantra</s>].
(KauśS 4.12[36].24) Without crushing.
(KauśS 4.12[36].25) With '<s>īrṣyāyā dhrājiṃ</s>' [AV 6.18.1], '<s>janād viśvajanīnāt</s>' [AV 7.45.1], '<s>tvāṣṭreṇāhaṃ</s>' [AV 7.74.3] — these are the counter-recitations, givings, and touchings.
(KauśS 4.12[36].26) With the first [verse], on the flanks, as stated in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4.12[36].27) With '<s>agner iva</s>' [AV 7.45.2] — an axe-blade.
(KauśS 4.12[36].28) With '<s>ava jyām iva</s>' [AV 6.42.1], having seen, he picks up a stone.
(KauśS 4.12[36].29) With the second [verse], he places [it] down.
(KauśS 4.12[36].30) With the third [verse], he spits upon [it].
(KauśS 4.12[36].31) In the shadow, he strings the bow.
(KauśS 4.12[36].32) With '<s>ayaṃ darbho</s>' [AV 6.43.1] — like an herb.

body.text: (KauśS_4,12[36].33) <agne jātān [7.34.1]> iti na vīraṃ janayet <prānyān [7.35.1]> iti na vijāyeta_ity aśvatarīmūtram aśmamaṇḍalābhyāṃ saṃghṛṣya bhakte_alaṃkāre
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4.12[36].33) With '<s>agne jātān</s>' [AV 7.34.1], [the rite for] 'she should not bear a hero'; with '<s>prānyān</s>' [AV 7.35.1], 'she should not give birth' — having ground she-mule's urine with two stone discs, [he mixes it] into the food [and] the adornment.
(KauśS 4.12[36].34) He examines the hair-parting.
(KauśS 4.12[36].35) With '<s>api vṛśca</s>' [AV 7.90.1], he recites against the wife's paramour.
(KauśS 4.12[36].36) At the impotent's place, he cuts a constraining bow.
(KauśS 4.12[36].37) He hurls a stone at the resting-place.
(KauśS 4.12[36].38) With '<s>tṛṣṭike</s>' [AV 7.113.1] — [the rite uses] <s>bāṇāparṇī</s> [plant].
(KauśS 4.12[36].39) With '<s>ā te dade</s>' [AV 7.114.1], he touches the items mentioned in the <s>mantra</s>.
(KauśS 4.12[36].40) And he recites, and again he recites.

body.text: (KauśS 4 Colophon) iti atharvavede kauśikasūtre caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: (KauśS 4, Colophon) Thus ends the fourth chapter in the <s>Kauśikasūtra</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.
(KauśS 5.1[37].1) With '<s>ambayo yanty</s>' [AV 1.4.1] — [these are the rites involving] milk-rice, grass-tuft, pillar, and <s>pāṭā</s> divinations.
(KauśS 5.1[37].2) The altar-divination [is performed] in battle.

(KauśS 5.1[37].3) With '<s>venas tat</s>' [AV 2.1.1], he gazes at a five-jointed arrow, a pot, a water-vessel, a pillar, a <s>kāmpīla</s> branch, a yoke, a fuel-stick, dice, the palms, twenty-one pebbles.

body.text: (KauśS_5,1[37].4) kumbhamahatena pariveṣṭyādhāya śayane vikṛte saṃpātān atinayati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 5.1[37].4) Having wrapped [it] with a large pot-cloth and having placed [it] on a deformed bed, he leads the remnants past [it].

body.text: (KauśS_5,1[37].5) anatīkāśam avachādyārajovitte kumāryau yena haretāṃ tato naṣṭam
body.translated_text: (KauśS 5.1[37].5) Having covered [it] so it is not visible to the sky, on a dustless path, two maidens [carry it] — wherever they would take it, from there [the lost object] has gone.
(KauśS 5.1[37].6) Likewise, with a plough, [and] with a witness.

body.text: (KauśS_5,1[37].7) loṣṭānāṃ kumārīm āha yam ichasi tam ādatsva_iti
body.translated_text: (KauśS 5.1[37].7) He says to a maiden regarding the clay lumps: 'Take whichever one you wish.'
(KauśS 5.1[37].8) A lump in [proper] shape or from an anthill [portends] good fortune.
(KauśS 5.1[37].9) [A lump] from a crossroads [indicates] a much-travelling woman.
(KauśS 5.1[37].10) [A lump] from a cremation ground — she will not live long.
(KauśS 5.1[37].11) 'Pour the handful of water' — he says.
(KauśS 5.1[37].12) If she throws [it] eastward, [it portends] good fortune.
(KauśS 5.2[38].1) With '<s>jarāyujaḥ</s>' [AV 1.12.1] — when bad weather approaches, he rises to oppose [it].
(KauśS 5.2[38].2) Verse by verse, with water-thunderbolts.
(KauśS 5.2[38].3) Taking a sword, a firebrand, and <s>kiṣkurū</s> [sticks].
(KauśS 5.2[38].4) Naked, wiping the forehead.
(KauśS 5.2[38].5) Having scraped [embers] to the outside, in a charcoal-pot, he offers <s>śigru</s>-pebbles.
(KauśS 5.2[38].6) He places <s>kerārka</s> [sticks].

body.text: (KauśS_5,2[38].7) varṣaparītaḥ pratilomakarṣitas triḥ parikramya khadāyām arkaṃ kṣipraṃ saṃvapati
body.translated_text: (KauśS 5.2[38].7) Surrounded by rain, dragged against the grain [of the hair], having circled three times, in a pit, he quickly sows <s>arka</s> [plant].
